QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_44

question.text: Assignment of exercised options to option writers is done on:

answer.text: Random basis to short positions in option contracts of the same series
First-in-first-out basis based on when positions were written
Pro-rata basis based on the size of short positions
Assigned to the writer with the largest short position first

explanation.text: The Logic: When long ITM option holders exercise, the clearing corporation automatically assigns those exercised options on a random basis to short positions in option contracts of the same series. Random assignment ensures fairness — no writer is systematically targeted. The Trap: Assignment is NOT FIFO or pro-rata. Random assignment means any short position in the same series can be assigned, regardless of when the position was written or its size. Note: "Same series" means the same underlying, expiry, strike, and option type (call/put). Writers should anticipate that any of their short positions in an ITM series may be assigned at expiry.
